feed/CONTEXT.md:3:The acquisition and retrieval half of the system's feed capability. It scrapes a fixed set of Providers for articles and live-blog updates, persists them, and serves them to consumers through `feedq`. It is the source of truth for acquired feed source material and its retrieval indexes, and for nothing else: notes, truth, verification, vendor facts, roster relevance, and memory live in other contexts. LLM-driven work of any kind (extraction, classification, validation, clustering, synthesis, enrichment) is out of scope here. ADR-0004 through ADR-0011 are implemented at their documented scope: `feedq retrieve` serves chunk-grain BM25 (span and Live-update chunks together) with a full per-hit ranking feature log and dereference, Feed mints stable Article refs, retains Revisions, rebuilds deterministic Chunk refs, reports article-scan Coverage, can link near-duplicates, and echoes live corpus state on every response. Public JSON carries only ref-based identity (`article_ref`, `revision`, `chunk_ref`); numeric article ids never cross the boundary. Article-grain plus chunk-grain rank fusion is retired, not future work. Weighted ranking (tier/aggregator/quality/recency multipliers) ships behind a checked-in config at BM25-parity; a gold nDCG@10 benchmark harness exists to decide whether it ships for real, but the owner's labeling pass and that ship decision remain future work, as does dense/hybrid retrieval.
feed/CONTEXT.md:35:The canonical downstream identity of an Article: `art-<yyyymmdd>-<hex8>`, minted once by Feed at first acquisition and deliberately meaningless (no publisher, title, or URL inside). It is the only article identity in the `feedq` JSON contract (ADR-0004, contract v3/ADR-0011): no numeric article id crosses that boundary. The markdown export's frontmatter still carries a legible file-derived `id` field for humans reading a file on disk; that is a file compatibility value, not a JSON identity, and no context may mint or derive
